speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. To begin understanding the source of your knee pain following increased activity, could you please tell me exactly where the pain is located and what specific movements make it worse?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you. Given the recent volleyball activity involving pivoting, does the pain localize specifically to the lateral (outer) aspect of your knee, and do you feel or hear a "pop" when the pain started?

REQUEST TEST: Knee_Lateral_Deltoid_Tenderness

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Negative for lateral deltoid tenderness; pain localized to the medial aspect of the tibia.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since the lateral side is clear, I need to check for the hallmark sign of a tibial stress injury or medial collateral ligament issue. Can you tell me if you have point tenderness directly over the medial tibial shaft when I press on it?

REQUEST TEST: Medial_Tibial_Tenderness

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Tenderness present over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (Shin Splints).
